DIRECT_CAPACITY_LIMITED.label: Intentional — Capacity Constrained
DIRECT_CAPACITY_LIMITED.copy: Your answers point to intentional decisions rather than a lack of intentionality. What may be limiting the picture is simpler and less personal: there is too little money left after necessary expenses to make all of the additional decisions you would otherwise make.

DIRECT_LIMITED_EVIDENCE_CAPACITY.label: Limited Evidence
DIRECT_LIMITED_EVIDENCE_CAPACITY.copy: There is not enough clean evidence to make a broad statement about your financial decision style. Why? Because when there is very little money left to direct, it becomes difficult to tell the difference between what you would choose and what your circumstances currently allow you to choose. So this part of your picture deserves some humility: limited financial room should not be mistaken for limited financial agency.

AIM_CAPACITY_CONSTRAINED_ALIGNMENT.label: Clear Direction — Limited Room to Act
AIM_CAPACITY_CONSTRAINED_ALIGNMENT.copy: You know where you want to go, and the destination itself is not the problem. What may be missing is the room: limited financial space can make it difficult for today's decisions to reflect that future as fully as you would like. This is a capacity constraint, not an absence of direction.

HIGH_ACTIVITY_LOW_DIRECTION.headline: A Lot Is Happening. The Destination Needs More Say.
HIGH_ACTIVITY_LOW_DIRECTION.body: You are making decisions and handling what is in front of you, but that activity is not always organized around a clearly defined destination. The opportunity may not be to do more. It may be to make the future you want a stronger filter for what gets your money today.

connection.headline: Activity Without a Say From the Future.
framing: The activity itself is not the problem — decisions are being made and things are getting handled. What is worth noticing is how few of those decisions ask the future first.
You do not need more motion. You need the destination you already sense to get a vote in today's choices.

HIGH_INFORMATION_LOW_ACTION.headline: You Have the Information. The Bridge to Action Is Missing.
HIGH_INFORMATION_LOW_ACTION.body: You can take in and evaluate financial information, but useful information does not always become follow-through. The friction appears to be between knowing and doing, not simply a lack of education. The question is not whether you understand — it is what stands between understanding and the next step.

connection.headline: The Distance Between Knowing and Doing.
framing: Two things are showing up together: you are able to take in financial information, and that information does not always travel all the way into action.
That gap is not a verdict on what you know. It is a place worth looking at closely — because the fix for a knowing problem and the fix for a doing problem look nothing alike.

INFORMATION_ANALYSIS_BOTTLENECK.headline: The Information Is Arriving. The Decision Process Is Crowded.
INFORMATION_ANALYSIS_BOTTLENECK.body: You are exposed to financial information, but evaluating competing advice can become difficult enough that action slows down. A clearer way to sort what is relevant may matter more than consuming more content. The bottleneck is not availability — it is the sorting.

connection.headline: Too Many Voices at the Decision.
framing: Information is reaching you. What is getting crowded is the part where you decide which of it applies to your life.
Once sorting becomes the hard step, adding more information adds weight rather than clarity. A simpler rule for what deserves attention may do more than another source.

INFORMATION_EXECUTION_BOTTLENECK.headline: You Can Evaluate It. The Next Step Keeps Slipping.
INFORMATION_EXECUTION_BOTTLENECK.body: You can generally sort and evaluate financial information, but follow-through is less consistent. The opportunity appears to be turning a sound decision into a concrete next action — small enough to do, soon enough to matter. Knowing what you would do is not the same as having done it.

connection.headline: The Last Step Is the One That Counts.
framing: Your evaluation looks sound. Where things slip is the handoff — the moment a good decision is supposed to become something you actually did.
That handoff is where intentions usually go quiet. Naming it as the friction, rather than as a character trait, is what makes it workable.

INFORMATION_OVERLOAD_PATTERN.headline: More Information Is Adding Noise, Not Clarity.
INFORMATION_OVERLOAD_PATTERN.body: Financial information can become overwhelming before it becomes useful. When too many voices compete at once, the next step may be a simpler process for deciding what deserves attention and what can be set aside. The volume, not the content, is what is getting in the way.

connection.headline: When More Information Becomes Less Clarity.
framing: There is a point where information stops informing and starts competing — and your answers suggest you have reached it.
The relief is not another source. It is a smaller queue: fewer things allowed to speak at once, so the ones that matter can be heard.

HIGH_VISIBILITY_LOW_CAPACITY.headline: Your Money Has Less Breathing Room Than Your Plans Need
HIGH_VISIBILITY_LOW_CAPACITY.body: A large share of your available dollars appears to already have a job before you get the opportunity to make additional choices with them. Limited margin does more than make a budget feel tight. It can reduce your ability to respond to opportunities, absorb surprises, accelerate a goal, or make one decision without another priority having to give something up. Visibility tells you what is happening. It does not automatically create flexibility.

connection.headline: Limited Room May Be the Common Thread.
framing: Three things that can look separate—day-to-day tradeoffs, slower movement toward the future, and less protection from disruption—may actually be connected by the same constraint: financial room.
You can see the picture. You have direction. And useful information often becomes movement for you.
But when too much of today's income is already committed, clarity cannot automatically become action.

That means the opportunity may not be to become more disciplined, consume more information, or want your goals more badly. It may be to create enough capacity for the discipline, clarity, and direction you already have to do more work.
And that same financial room matters twice: it gives you more freedom to move toward what you want and more ability to recover when life moves against the plan. That is the connection worth noticing.

LOW_VISIBILITY_HIGH_CAPACITY.headline: You Have Room. The Picture Needs More Detail.
LOW_VISIBILITY_HIGH_CAPACITY.body: There appears to be some financial flexibility available to you, while the day-to-day picture is not yet as visible as it could be. Room without a clear view makes it harder to decide what the available money should accomplish — the opportunity is clarity, not more income.

connection.headline: Room Is Waiting on a Clearer Picture.
framing: The two halves of this pattern pull in opposite directions: the money is there, and the map of it is thin.
That is good news in an odd wrapper. Flexibility is the harder thing to build; visibility is the faster thing to fix — and a clearer picture is what lets the room start working on purpose.

HIGH_DIRECTION_LOW_CAPACITY.headline: Your Direction Is Clear. Your Dollars Have Less Freedom to Follow.
HIGH_DIRECTION_LOW_CAPACITY.body: You know where you want to go, but the present appears to be consuming enough financial capacity that the future does not always get as much of your money as it gets of your attention. That creates a particular kind of tension: the goal is not missing; the ability to consistently fund the goal is what is under pressure.

connection.headline: The Destination Is Not Missing. The Margin Is.
framing: You know what you want money to make possible, and today's dollars are largely spoken for before they can move toward it.
This is a funding gap, not a motivation gap. Attention and money are currently pointing in different directions — which is exactly the kind of tension that eases when room is made on purpose.

HIGH_FEAR_HIGH_ACTIVATION.headline: The Concern Is Real. So Is Your Readiness to Move.
HIGH_FEAR_HIGH_ACTIVATION.body: Fear or hesitation shows up around some of your financial decisions, while your urgency, readiness, or commitment to make progress is also strong. Both can be true at the same time. The goal is not to create more pressure; it is to make the next decision feel informed and owned by you.

connection.headline: Careful and Ready at the Same Time.
framing: Two things that often cancel each other are both present: real caution about getting it wrong, and genuine readiness to move.
That combination works when the caution is aimed at the decision rather than at motion itself. The next step can be both careful and yours.

SUPPORT_OPENNESS_AGENCY_VULNERABILITY.headline: Open to Help — and Protective of the Wheel.
SUPPORT_OPENNESS_AGENCY_VULNERABILITY.body: You are open to professional support, while asking questions or challenging a recommendation may be less comfortable. Useful guidance should increase your understanding and decision ownership, not replace it. The test of any support is whether you understand your options better afterward.

connection.headline: Guidance Should Widen, Not Replace, the Decision.
framing: You are open to being helped, and you are less practiced at pushing back — those two facts often arrive together.
The standard worth holding: support that leaves you more able to decide for yourself has done its job. Support that asks you to hand the decision over has not.

HEALTHY_PRIVACY_BOUNDARY.headline: Selective About What You Share — and Still Willing to Look.
HEALTHY_PRIVACY_BOUNDARY.body: You are selective about what financial information you share, while still being willing to look at your numbers and ask questions when needed. That pattern can reflect a healthy privacy boundary rather than financial avoidance. Discretion and honesty with yourself are not in tension.

connection.headline: Private Does Not Mean Avoidant.
framing: There is a version of privacy that protects a boundary and a version that postpones a hard conversation — and your answers point at the first.
You are willing to look. What you share, and with whom, stays yours to choose. Those are separate decisions, and you are treating them that way.

PRIVACY_AVOIDANCE_FRICTION.headline: Privacy May Be Sitting on Top of Avoidance.
PRIVACY_AVOIDANCE_FRICTION.body: Keeping financial information private may sometimes show up alongside discomfort looking at the numbers or concern about judgment. One possibility worth examining is whether privacy is protecting a healthy boundary in some moments and making it easier to postpone a difficult conversation in others.

connection.headline: When the Boundary Also Becomes the Wall.
framing: Privacy is doing real work for you — and it may also be giving certain numbers a place to stay unexamined.
The distinction to notice is not public versus private. It is whether the keeping-private is a choice you are making, or a habit making itself.

HIGH_CONFIDENCE_LOW_VISIBILITY.headline: Confidence Is Present. The Picture Needs More Evidence.
HIGH_CONFIDENCE_LOW_VISIBILITY.body: There is confidence in evaluating financial information, while parts of your own financial picture remain less visible. Bringing those two together may help ensure that confidence is grounded in the numbers that matter most to your situation. Capability is not the question; the evidence it has to work with is.

connection.headline: Strong Judgment, Thin Evidence.
framing: You trust yourself to evaluate money questions — and parts of your own numbers are still outside the frame.
That combination is workable precisely because the capable half is already in place. Grounding the view in your own figures is the step that lets good judgment do good work.

PREPAREDNESS_KNOWLEDGE_LOW_RESILIENCE.headline: Your Awareness of Risk Is Ahead of the Cushion
PREPAREDNESS_KNOWLEDGE_LOW_RESILIENCE.body: You have already thought about what a meaningful financial disruption could do. The vulnerability appears further downstream: whether enough resources, flexibility, or recovery capacity would be available if something actually interrupted the plan. Knowing that a risk exists and being financially positioned to absorb it are two different things. Your awareness appears to be ahead of the cushion.

connection.headline: The Thinking Is Done. The Cushion Is the Question.
framing: You have already done the part most people avoid: you know what a disruption would mean. What is still open is whether the resources on hand would match the plan in your head.
Awareness without a cushion is not a flaw — it is a head start pointing at a specific next question: what would absorb the interruption, and how much of that exists today?

BIG_PICTURE_CASHFLOW_GAP.headline: The Big Picture Is Clear. The Monthly Flow Is Not.
BIG_PICTURE_CASHFLOW_GAP.body: You can describe your finances at a high level, while the month-to-month movement of money is harder to account for. Closing that gap may make the larger picture more actionable — the overview is the easy half; the flow is where decisions actually happen.

connection.headline: You Know the Shape. The Flow Is Fuzzy.
framing: The overview version of your finances is available to you; the monthly version is harder to reconstruct.
That gap matters because most financial decisions are made at the monthly level, not the overview level. What is visible from above deserves a closer look from inside the month.

DESTINATION_EXISTS_ACTIVITY_NOT_ORGANIZE.headline: You Know Where You Want to Go. Today Is Not Organized Around It.
DESTINATION_EXISTS_ACTIVITY_NOT_ORGANIZE.body: The destination itself is not the problem. You can describe what you want money to make possible, but day-to-day financial activity may still be organized around immediate demands rather than that destination. The future has your answer — it just does not yet have much of your calendar or your dollars.

connection.headline: The Destination Has Your Answer. Not Yet Your Calendar.
framing: You can say what you want money to make possible. What does not yet match that answer is the way ordinary weeks are arranged.
Reorganizing is not about effort — it is about letting the destination you already have choose between competing demands sooner, rather than later.

CLEAR_DESTINATION_CAPACITY_CONSTRAINED_A.headline: The Goal Is Clear. The Margin to Fund It Is Not.
CLEAR_DESTINATION_CAPACITY_CONSTRAINED_A.body: Several of your answers describe the same squeeze from different angles: what you intend for the money and what the month allows it to do are running on different budgets. The plan is not short on intent — it is short on uncommitted dollars. Until margin opens, the future keeps getting funded last, with whatever is left.

connection.headline: The Destination Is Not Missing. The Margin Is.
framing: Your direction is not the open question. What is open is how much of today's money can actually travel toward it.
When margin is the constraint, decisions start reflecting the bills before they reflect the future you described. That is a spacing problem — and spacing problems respond to deliberate room-making.

NO_MEANINGFUL_FRICTION_IDENTIFIED.headline: Nothing Here Needs to Be Invented.
NO_MEANINGFUL_FRICTION_IDENTIFIED.body: Your responses do not point to one meaningful area of friction that clearly explains the rest of your financial picture. That does not mean there is nothing to improve. It means this assessment should not manufacture a problem that your responses do not support.

connection.headline: No Single Pressure Worth Naming.
framing: Nothing in this picture insists on being called a problem, and this Snapshot will not invent one.
What is here instead is a set of working parts — some sharper than others — worth continuing to observe rather than to fix on schedule.

context_narratives.CRISIS_BASED_MONEY_CONVERSATION: You describe money conversations as something that tended to happen when there was a problem, concern, or immediate need.
context_narratives.CONFLICTING_MONEY_MESSAGES: You describe receiving mixed or conflicting messages about money. That context may be useful when considering which beliefs still fit the life you want now.
context_narratives.LIMITED_MONEY_CONVERSATION: You describe money as something that was not discussed very much in the environment where you grew up.
context_narratives.INCOME_PRESSURE: You identified income as one contributor when money feels tight.
context_narratives.LOW_AVAILABLE_MONEY: You identified having little or no money left after regular bills as one contributor to financial pressure.
context_narratives.DEBT_PRESSURE: You identified debt payments as one contributor to financial pressure.
context_narratives.MAJOR_FIXED_COST_PRESSURE: You identified major fixed costs such as housing, childcare, or transportation as one contributor to financial pressure.
context_narratives.COST_OF_LIVING_PRESSURE: You identified everyday costs as one contributor to financial pressure.

PERCEPTION_ALIGNED.headline: Your Starting View Was Largely Aligned
PERCEPTION_ALIGNED.body: How financially Set for Life you felt at the beginning appears broadly consistent with the patterns that showed up across the assessment.

PERCEPTION_MORE_OPTIMISTIC_THAN_PROFILE.headline: Your Starting View Was More Optimistic Than Some of the Patterns
PERCEPTION_MORE_OPTIMISTIC_THAN_PROFILE.body: You began with a stronger sense of being financially Set for Life than some of the patterns in your responses suggest. This is not a correction of your self-view; it is an invitation to notice where confidence and current conditions may not be telling exactly the same story.

PERCEPTION_MORE_CAUTIOUS_THAN_PROFILE.headline: You May Be Giving Yourself Less Credit Than the Patterns Support
PERCEPTION_MORE_CAUTIOUS_THAN_PROFILE.body: You began with a more cautious view of how financially Set for Life you feel, while several of your responses show strengths that may be more developed than your starting impression suggested.

PERCEPTION_MIXED_COMPLEX.headline: Your Starting View and Your Responses Tell a More Layered Story
PERCEPTION_MIXED_COMPLEX.body: Your starting sense of being financially Set for Life does not reduce neatly to more or less confident. Some parts of your financial life appear stronger while others carry meaningful friction. The mixed picture is the finding.

body: This does not feel urgent to you right now — and the honest read is that it does not have to be. There is real value in looking at your financial life while there is still room to choose what changes, and when.
Nothing here expires. What matters more than speed is that the look is honest.
This does not feel especially urgent to you right now.
And it does not have to.
There is value in being able to look at your financial life before everything becomes a crisis.
Making meaningful progress soon feels important to you right now.
That sense of timing is useful information rather than pressure. The work is aiming it — so the urgency is spent on the changes that matter, not on everything at once.
You do not feel ready to take a closer look or make changes right now.
That is a legitimate position, and nothing in this Snapshot argues with it. When the moment shifts, the picture will still be here to read.
You are willing to take a closer look.
Your readiness to make changes is still forming, which makes understanding what actually deserves attention more important than trying to change everything at once.
You are ready to look closely and make changes where they make sense.
Readiness at this level works best when it has somewhere specific to land — knowing what deserves attention first keeps the willingness from scattering across everything.
Following through consistently on a financial change does not feel realistic or desirable for you right now.
That is worth knowing plainly rather than planning around. Any next step worth taking should assume the support it actually needs.
You will follow through when a change genuinely makes sense for your life — though consistency may still need some support.
That is a workable position: the willingness is real, and the conditions around it matter. Well-chosen changes fit your life more easily than impressive ones.
When a financial change makes sense for your life, you believe you can stay with it.
That willingness is an asset.
The goal is not simply to work harder. It is to make sure your effort is aimed at the right problem.

LOW.stateLabel: Not Looking for Guidance Right Now
body: You would rather not explore professional guidance right now.
That is a clear preference and a complete answer. This Snapshot is built to be useful without it — everything here stands on its own.
You may be open to professional guidance if the fit, trust, and value are clear.
The condition is the sensible part. Guidance worth having has to earn the place — and being open to it commits you to nothing.

HIGH.stateLabel: Open When the Fit Is Right
body: You are open to professional guidance when it feels clear, trustworthy, useful, and worth the value.
Being open to guidance is not the same as handing over the decision.
The right support should help you understand your options well enough to remain the owner of your choices.

SEE_IT_MORE_CLEARLY.label: SEE IT MORE CLEARLY
body: If you examine one thing next, examine visibility. The goal is not perfect tracking — it is enough clarity to know what is happening and what deserves attention first. When the picture is visible, decisions get faster and easier to trust. Make the financial life easier to see before trying to change it.

CREATE_MORE_ROOM.label: CREATE MORE ROOM
body: If you examine one thing next, examine financial room.
Across your Snapshot, the recurring constraint is not that you lack awareness, direction, or a willingness to make thoughtful decisions.
It is how much flexibility remains after the dollars that are already committed have done their jobs.
Creating more room does not automatically mean: spend less, sacrifice more, squeeze the same dollars harder.
What would have to change for more of your income to become available for the life you are trying to build?
That may eventually lead you to examine expenses, obligations, timing, income—or some combination of them.
For now, the insight is simpler.
More room creates more choices.

STRENGTHEN_RESILIENCE.label: STRENGTHEN RESILIENCE
body: As financial room improves, keep an eye on how much of that increased flexibility is available to absorb the unexpected—not only fund the expected.

DEFINE_THE_DESTINATION.label: DEFINE THE DESTINATION
body: If you examine one thing next, examine what you want your money to make possible. A clearer destination lets current decisions compete on purpose instead of urgency alone — and it turns vague progress into directional progress. The destination does not have to be final to start doing this work.

TURN_INFORMATION_INTO_ACTION.label: TURN INFORMATION INTO ACTION
body: If you examine one thing next, examine where useful financial information loses momentum. The next step may be less about learning more and more about making one informed decision concrete enough to act on — small enough to do, soon enough to matter.

BUILD_DECISION_CONFIDENCE.label: BUILD DECISION CONFIDENCE
body: If you examine one thing next, examine how you make decisions when the answer is not obvious. Strong decision confidence includes asking questions, understanding tradeoffs, protecting healthy boundaries — and keeping ownership of the final decision, whoever else is in the room.

KEEP_OBSERVING.label: KEEP OBSERVING WHAT IS WORKING
body: Your responses do not support inventing a problem. A useful next step is to keep observing what is working, where conditions change, and whether any new friction becomes meaningful over time. Nothing here needs fixing on a schedule; it needs noticing.

rules: Never expose raw 1–5 values to participants.
Never describe low capacity as low discipline or low agency.
Never infer causation from correlation or classifier co-occurrence.
Every personalized statement must resolve to a stored narrative key and evidence chain.
A4 never changes diagnosis and never constitutes appointment, marketing, or purchase consent.
If no meaningful friction is supported, use NO_MEANINGFUL_FRICTION_IDENTIFIED.
If Q11_A and Q12_F both trigger, use DIRECT_LIMITED_EVIDENCE_CAPACITY rather than a low DIRECT state.
If Direction is clear, alignment is low, and Capacity is constrained, prefer AIM_CAPACITY_CONSTRAINED_ALIGNMENT / CLEAR_DESTINATION_CAPACITY_CONSTRAINED_ALIGNMENT.
Context classifiers are descriptive and may be omitted from the participant-facing report when they do not materially improve understanding.

default.headline: The Question Is Room, Not Will.
body: The central tension in your Snapshot is not effort or intention — it is capacity. When most of the dollars coming in are already spoken for, even thoughtful decisions become tradeoffs.
The question worth carrying out of this page is simple: what would have to change for the room you already have to work harder for the future you already want?

CREATE_MORE_ROOM.headline: You See the Picture. The Challenge Is Having Enough Room to Move.
body: You have a strong sense of the direction you want your money to take you. The central tension in your Snapshot is not awareness. It is capacity.

When most of the dollars coming in are already spoken for, even thoughtful decisions can become tradeoffs. That can slow progress toward the future, reduce flexibility in the present, and make the unexpected harder to absorb.
Your Snapshot points less toward “I need to know more” and more toward a different question:
How do I create enough financial room for what I already know to begin working harder for me?

KEEP_OBSERVING.headline: Effort Is Not the Constraint. Room Is.
body: Nothing here points to a weakness in how you manage money — what it points to is a tight margin. With most income already committed, the picture reads as capable hands working in a narrow space.
The question this Snapshot leaves you with is not how to try harder, but how to widen the space your decisions have to work in.

default.headline: One Pressure Is Carrying Most of the Story.
body: Put together, your Snapshot has a clear center of gravity: one area is creating more pressure than the rest, and the other findings tend to lean on it.
Naming that center is the point of this page — so attention can go where it changes the most, rather than everywhere at once.

TURN_INFORMATION_INTO_ACTION.headline: You Know a Great Deal. The Missing Piece Is Movement.
body: Your answers show a person who can take in financial information and evaluate it well. What they show less of is that information consistently becoming a next step.

That puts the friction between knowing and doing — and it reframes the question. More information is unlikely to be the answer; the question is what would let a sound decision become something you actually did.

SEE_IT_MORE_CLEARLY.headline: The Picture Is Uneven Where It Matters Most.
body: Your Snapshot reads as capable in many places and uneven in one: some regions are visible, and some important ones are not.
That gap is the pressure — decisions are being made with a map that has blank areas on it. The question worth asking first is what would make the missing parts visible.

default.headline: A Steady, Developing Picture.
body: Nothing in your responses points to one area that needs to take center stage right now. Several threads are still taking shape.
That is a real finding, not a missing one: this Snapshot will not manufacture a problem your answers do not support. What is here is worth keeping an eye on rather than fixing on schedule.

default.headline: A Picture Still Coming Into Focus.
body: Nothing in your responses is weak, and nothing is fully settled either. The picture reads as developing rather than fixed — several parts are taking shape, and the shape itself is the finding.
That makes this a good moment to keep observing: what strengthens over the next few months will tell you more than any single answer does today.

money-picture: Six questions. Six parts of one financial picture.
None of these stands alone, and none is a grade. Read together, they show where your financial life feels clear, where it has room, and where something may be getting in the way.
strengths: These are the parts of your financial life that are already carrying weight for you — the ground you can build on.
friction: Clarity is not the problem here. The tighter spots appear where what you know, what you want, and what your current financial capacity allows are not fully lining up yet.
readiness: Readiness does not always move in a straight line.
You can be clear in one area, cautious in another, and fully prepared to act when the right change becomes obvious. These four signals simply show what is true for you right now.

What the evidence supports here is

signal_strengths.SEE: Clarity at this level is not common, and it shortens the distance between noticing something and acting on it. Visibility like yours is a working advantage — it is what makes every other decision faster.
signal_strengths.ROOM: This kind of flexibility is the buffer that keeps one unexpected month from becoming a crisis, and it is what funds choices that are not emergencies. Protecting it matters as much as spending it.
signal_strengths.DIRECT: Deciding with purpose — weighing tradeoffs instead of responding to whichever demand is loudest — is the difference between money that follows a plan and money that follows the week.
signal_strengths.PREPARE: You have already done the thinking that most people postpone: you know what could go wrong and you have built room to answer it. That preparation is quiet, but it is doing real work.
signal_strengths.AIM: A clear destination is the rarest asset in this picture — many people cannot say what they want money to make possible. Yours is doing real work already, steering decisions before this Snapshot even named it.
signal_strengths.MOVE: The path from knowing to doing is intact for you. When something makes sense, it becomes a decision — which means new information actually lands instead of accumulating.
